headline: Medium prompt-injection and cascading-error risk via MCP-to-PDF workflow; no direct data-leak or compliance breach is evidenced.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: MemMachine exposes an MCP Server and REST/Python interfaces, while pdf.js processes PDF files and can run browser-based tests. A plausible pairwise path is content from PDFs or browser-rendered documents being fed into MemMachine through MCP, where instruction-like text could be treated as trusted context. The interaction is inferred, not directly documented, so uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than low.
conditions: IF pdf.js output is forwarded into MemMachine's MCP or REST input without provenance tagging, injection risk exists.
IF MemMachine treats document text as instructions or memory, attacker-controlled PDF content can steer behavior.
mitigations: Add a manual review step before forwarding PDF-derived text to MemMachine.
Prefix all PDF-derived content with a non-executable provenance label.
Disable automatic ingestion from browser-rendered document text.
Use a separate workspace for untrusted PDFs.
requires-engineering: add provenance-aware parsing between pdf.js and MemMachine.

B_data_leakage.rationale: MemMachine touches long-term user facts and conversational context and has allowlisted network egress; pdf.js touches PDF documents and has no network egress. The profiles do not show a shared filesystem, shared OAuth principal, or uncontrolled upload path, so a direct leakage pathway is not established. The main concern is limited local exposure if operators manually move PDFs into MemMachine.
conditions: IF operators copy PDF contents into MemMachine prompts or memory, those contents may be retained with user context.
IF a shared workspace is introduced outside the profiles, leakage risk increases.
mitigations: Keep pdf.js and MemMachine in separate directories.
Avoid pasting full PDF text into MemMachine unless necessary.
Redact sensitive fields before transfer.
Review MemMachine memory entries after document processing.
requires-engineering: enforce workspace isolation and access controls.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: MemMachine has allowlisted network egress and MCP/API surfaces, while pdf.js supports browser-based tests and multiple instances but no filesystem write or mutable shared-resource scope is documented. There is no evidence of overlapping write access to the same directory, git state, or OAuth scopes, so a true capability conflict is not demonstrated. Uncertainty remains because the orchestrator and deployment topology are undocumented.
conditions: IF both agents are granted write access to the same mutable workspace, conflicts can occur.
IF an external orchestrator adds shared locks or shared state, the conflict profile changes.
mitigations: Assign separate working directories.
Avoid concurrent writes to shared artifacts.
Run pdf.js as read-only where possible.
Document ownership of any shared files.
requires-engineering: add locking for shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: MemMachine can ingest conversational context and long-term user facts, and pdf.js produces document-processing outputs that may be treated as authoritative by downstream automation. If pdf.js-derived text is passed into MemMachine without verification, MemMachine can amplify extraction errors into persistent memory or later actions. The pairwise pathway is plausible from the profiles, though not directly observed.
conditions: IF pdf.js extraction output is stored in MemMachine memory without human verification, errors can persist.
IF downstream workflows act on MemMachine memory as authoritative, incorrect document facts can cascade.
mitigations: Verify extracted facts against the source PDF before saving.
Store raw PDF references alongside summaries.
Mark unverified fields as provisional.
Limit automatic actions based on newly ingested document facts.
requires-engineering: add confidence scoring and verification gates.

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and the documented data classes are general user facts and PDF documents, with no PHI, EU-only residency, or retention mismatch stated. Because no compliance-sensitive residency or certification conflict is evidenced, only a low residual compliance concern remains from handling user documents and memory together. The other agent is cited because the risk is pairwise data handling, not a single-agent residency issue.
conditions: IF PDFs contain regulated data classes not declared in the profiles, compliance obligations may apply.
IF MemMachine retains document-derived personal data longer than policy allows, retention mismatch can arise.
mitigations: Classify incoming PDFs before ingestion.
Set a retention policy for memory entries.
Avoid storing regulated data in long-term memory.
Review deletion/export workflows.
requires-engineering: implement policy-based retention controls.
